newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's 1996 disaster death toll nears 1,000.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's 1996 disaster death toll nears 1,000.

text.p: Almost 1,000 people have died in nine natural disasters in Vietnam so far this year, the country's worst in a decade for flooding and tropical storms, a U.N.-sponsored relief agency said on Thursday.
The Disaster Management Unit (DMU) said 965 people had been killed, more than a third as a result of recent flooding in the Mekong Delta and the central provinces.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Crescent Societies in Hanoi said worldwide appeals had been launched for relief funds totalling $1.77 million, one for storm-ravaged northern provinces and one for the Mekong Delta.
"For the Mekong I think you have to go back to 1978," an official with the federation said, referring to the last time flooding in Vietnam's southern rice bowl had been so severe.
The DMU said more than 828,000 households had been affected by flooding in the Mekong Delta, one in five of which were in need of relief.
Some 250,000 hectares (617,750 acres) of the region's paddy fields were under water, more than 10 percent of which had been completely destroyed, it said.
Total damage from the country's natural disasters this year was estimated at $628 million.
